questions.subject: Arrhythmias
questions.question: Which of the following is the first-line rate control agent in a hemodynamically stable patient with atrial fibrillation and intact left ventricular systolic function?
questions.explanation: Beta-blockers (such as metoprolol) or non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are first-line agents for rate control in atrial fibrillation with preserved ejection fraction.

questions.subject: Ischemic Heart Disease
questions.question: A 58-year-old male presents with crushing chest pain. The ECG reveals ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Which coronary artery is most likely occluded?
questions.explanation: Leads II, III, and aVF represent the inferior myocardial wall, which is supplied by the Right Coronary Artery (RCA) in approximately 85–90% of individuals.
